plan_a_advantages: Dedicated tempo session for threshold development.
Longer, controlled runs to build endurance and trail durability.
More focused on building speed-related physiological adaptations.
plan_b_advantages: Higher overall volume of running mileage.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more targeted approach to building both aerobic base and threshold strength, crucial for improving speed on trails. Plan B focuses heavily on maintaining freshness and volume, which is valuable but doesn't directly address the primary goal of increasing speed. Plan A’s inclusion of a dedicated tempo session and longer, controlled efforts will provide a more effective stimulus for physiological adaptations that translate to faster running, while Plan B’s longer, moderate-intensity runs could lead to fatigue and hinder progress.
